clue.text: American poet nominally of high standing

explanation.surface: A note about a poet from the United States whose very name suggests eminence.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's surname, split as a phrase, describes a tall man, which is what 'nominally of high standing' means: standing high in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow wrote Hiawatha; his surname taken literally describes a tall chap, someone who stands high.

clue.text: Behold an advance!

parts.note: lo is the old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at an upfront payment arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan is money advanced to someone, so the noun advance is a synonym.

clue.text: Nothing to worry about: it's not Russian money

parts.note: taken as written
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Reassurance that there is no cause for concern, since the cash is not Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for an easy task or no bother at all, nothing to worry about.

clue.text: Practise sword-play round the enclosure

explanation.surface: Fencers practise their swordsmanship around a paddock.
explanation.definitionFit: To fence is to fight with foils as a sport; a fence is also a barrier enclosing a field.

clue.text: Terpsichorean troops

parts.note: soldiers armed with long spears share a name with a set of quadrilles, a ballroom dance; Terpsichore is the Muse of dancing

explanation.surface: Soldiers who dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Terpsichore was the Greek Muse of dance, so 'Terpsichorean' means to do with dancing; the Lancers was a popular 19th-century square dance, and lancers are also cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry who carried lances gave their name to a 19th-century square dance, so both troops and a dance fit.

clue.text: Playful pillow-fighter to return greeting

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: hello is a common greeting

explanation.surface: A frolicsome child in a pillow fight is told to say hi in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' means 'from a play': Shakespeare's Moor smothers Desdemona with a pillow. 'return' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic Moor kills his wife Desdemona by smothering her with a pillow, a grim pillow-fight on stage.

clue.text: Money earned to carry on war

explanation.surface: Pay received for fighting a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay for work is a weekly earning; one also speaks of waging a war or campaign, meaning carrying it on.

clue.text: A little gentleman as someone's representative

parts.note: gent is the shortened form of gentleman, so a little version of the word

explanation.surface: A small man acting on behalf of another person.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts for a client, as their representative in business or negotiations.

clue.text: Where to look for Cockneys in South Africa

definitions.text: Where to look for Cockneys in South Africa

parts.words: Where to look for Cockneys in South Africa
parts.note: Cockneys live in the eastern part of the British capital, and a port city in the Eastern Cape bears the same name

explanation.surface: Searching for Londoners abroad in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are traditional working-class Londoners from the East End; East London is also a port city in South Africa's Eastern Cape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cockney heartland is the eastern part of the British capital, and a South African port shares that place name.

clue.text: Make a song about steam engineer killing flies

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for making a song wraps round the engineer

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about an engineer who keeps swatting insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' reads as 'make a fuss', but 'about' is the container signal: WATT goes inside SING as S-WATT-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swatting is hitting insects with a flat swat, so it describes killing flies.

clue.text: Continue to perform in West London

explanation.surface: An actor keeps working in a West London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on is to keep acting or performing; Acton is a district in the London Borough of Ealing.

clue.text: Exclusive notice for falconers

parts.note: a sign on a gate keeping out door-to-door pedlars, read as banning people who fly birds of prey

explanation.surface: A sign announcing something only for people who keep hawks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' looks like 'for members only', but the notice excludes: the sign banning pedlars from a doorway is read as if it barred falconers, who also hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawkers are street pedlars, and such a sign shuts them out; falconers also hawk, flying hawks at game.

clue.text: N.B,--observe hole in ground

parts.note: to note is to observe or take notice of
a well is a hole sunk in the ground for water

explanation.surface: A memo flags a hole in the ground to look out for.
explanation.walkthrough: N.B. stands for the Latin nota bene, mark well.
explanation.definitionFit: N.B. abbreviates the Latin nota bene, an instruction to mark carefully what follows.

clue.text: The end of the summer's work?

definitions.text: The end of the summer's work?

parts.words: The end of the summer's work?
parts.note: summer here is one who sums, an adder of figures, and the result reached at the end of the adding up

explanation.surface: Asks what is achieved by the close of the warm season's labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who does sums; what they arrive at at the end is the sum of the figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adding a column of figures finishes by writing down the sum, the overall amount.

clue.text: Gilbertian girl's confession reveals impetuosity

parts.note: the girl's confession is her declaring who she is, I am, contracted
Patience is the title heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

explanation.surface: A heroine from a comic opera makes a confession that shows her hot-headedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience (1881) is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta named for its milkmaid heroine; her confession 'I'm Patience' gives the opposite quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuosity is rash eagerness, being unwilling to wait, which is a lack of composure.

clue.text: Headwear for the rabble

parts.note: soft frilled caps once worn indoors by women, read as hats for the mob

explanation.surface: Hats issued to the common crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A mob cap is an old-fashioned soft cap with a frill; split the word and it reads as caps for a mob, the rabble.
explanation.definitionFit: These soft indoor caps were worn by women in the 18th century; mob is a word for the rabble.

clue.text: In art bundles of hay provide equipment for a cross bowman

indicators.note: in places the bundles inside the word art

parts.note: taken as written
bales are tied bundles of hay

explanation.surface: Bales of hay in an artwork supply gear for an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbalest is a medieval crossbow, the weapon of a crossbowman.

clue.text: Circular flight feather for personal assessment

parts.note: the letter O is circular in shape
a pinion is a bird's outer wing feather used for flight

explanation.surface: A round feather used to judge someone's view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or judgement someone holds is their own assessment of a matter.

clue.text: All the same, it changes in dialect

indicators.note: changes says the letters of in dialect are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Language shifts with regional dialect, yet stays the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike are all the same as one another.

clue.text: Beer, with medico in charge, produces such a retort

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A drink with a doctor in charge results in a sharp reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retort' reads as a sharp answer, but it is a glass vessel for distilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, a type of retort or still used by alchemists.

clue.text: Motor down to Yorkshire A river for a tipsy party

parts.note: motor is an old word for a car
the Ouse is a river that flows through York

explanation.surface: Driving down to a northern river for a drunken get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse flows through York in northern England. The stray 'A' looks like an OCR artefact of the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouse is a noisy drinking bout, a boozy party.

clue.text: Reg Cole, alias the Spanish Greek — artful chap!

indicators.note: an alias is an assumed name, a disguise, so the letters of Reg Cole take on a new form

explanation.surface: A man called Reg Cole is going under the name of a Spanish painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cretan-born painter Domenikos Theotokopoulos worked in Toledo and was nicknamed 'the Greek' in Spanish; 'artful chap' means an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan painter who worked in Toledo was known by a Spanish nickname meaning the Greek; he was an artist.

clue.text: The Red Viking about to desert? It's irregular

indicators.note: about means around, so the Viking's name surrounds the word for deserting

parts.note: Eric the Red was the Norse explorer who founded settlements in Greenland
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a famous Norse warrior is about to abandon his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric the Red was the tenth-century Norse explorer of Greenland; RAT goes inside ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is unpredictable or unsteady, lacking a regular pattern.

clue.text: Force latent in limp elastic

indicators.note: latent means lying concealed, so the letters are tucked away inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Notes that limp elastic holds a latent tension.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone onward is to drive or urge them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Beg for soft metal

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
lead is a heavy metal

explanation.surface: Asking for a soft metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to entreat earnestly, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Scarce portions from Wales make tasty snacks

parts.note: rare means scarce or uncommon
bits are small portions

explanation.surface: Uncommon helpings from Wales turn out to be delicious nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Wales' points to Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese sauce on toast, a savoury snack.

clue.text: Uncovered sliced bread

indicators.note: sliced bread is cut up, so its letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bread with its wrapper taken off and cut into slices.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid open is exposed or stripped, uncovered.

clue.text: Thus and thus in a mediocre way way

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
so again means thus

explanation.surface: Doing things one way and then another, but only adequately.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue repeats 'way', an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adverb means only passably or moderately, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Requires unfermented grape juice when the Devil drives

parts.note: needs means requires
must is freshly pressed grape juice before fermentation

explanation.surface: Winemaking needs fresh juice, as the proverb about the devil says.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'needs must when the devil drives' means necessity forces one's hand; the clue gives its missing first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The full proverb is 'needs must when the devil drives': the clue supplies the second half, the answer the first.

clue.text: Right page in correct order

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words correct order

explanation.surface: A page placed on the right in the proper sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, opposite the verso.

clue.text: Concluding stages in the Southend sprint

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie within the words Southend sprint

explanation.surface: The final phases of a race held in Southend, an Essex seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is a resort town in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: The finishing parts of a race or process are its last stages.

clue.text: Police clad in disorderly style? It's just a trivial offence

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters of police and clad are jumbled

explanation.surface: Scruffily dressed police commit only a minor misdemeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or minor fault, a trivial wrongdoing.
